sections.title: Root rules, memory table, and practice

steps.title: Root rules and roots to know
steps.intro: The rules, plus a roots table: blue cells are must-know, white cells are good to know.

tables.title: Rules
head: Rule
Note
rows: a root is a fractional power

tips: Number over a root: \(\frac6{\sqrt3}=2\sqrt3\) — ignore the root, then put it back.
Inside a square root: never negative.

explanation: Evaluate each cube root: ∛8 = 2 , ∛0 = 0 , and ∛(−1) = −1 (odd roots of negatives exist). Then 2 − 0 − (−1) = 2 + 1 = 3 .
An even-index root of a negative number has no real value: any real number raised to the sixth power is non-negative , so nothing to the sixth power equals −64 .
A root is a fractional exponent: ∛(5⁶) = 5^(6:3) = 5² = 25 .
A 1:4 exponent is a fourth root: 81^(1:4) = ⁴√81 = 3 , since 3⁴ = 81 .
Merge the product under one root: √27 · √3 = √(27·3) = √81 = 9 .
By definition, a square root times itself returns the number under the root: √31 · √31 = 31 .
Three copies of a cube root multiply back to the number under it: (∛9)³ = 9 .
Combine into a single root: √50:√2 = √(50:2) = √25 = 5 .

steps.stem: Evaluate \(\sqrt[2.5]{\sqrt{243}}\). Here the fractional root index \(2.5\) means raising to the power \(\frac{1}{2.5}\), i.e. \(\sqrt[2.5]{\sqrt{243}} = \left(\sqrt{243}\right)^{\frac{1}{2.5}}\) (the radicand is positive).
explanation: Use fractional exponents: (243^(1:2))^(1:2.5) = 243^(1:5) = 3, because 243 = 3^5. This is an extension of the integer-index root rules; the positive input makes the real-valued interpretation unambiguous.
Bring the 3 inside the root by squaring it: 3·√7 = √9 · √7 = √(9·7) = √63 .
To enter a cube root, the 3 must be cubed: 3·∛2 = ∛27 · ∛2 = ∛(27·2) = ∛54 .

steps.stem: Which of the following is the smallest?
explanation: Estimate each: √7 ≈ 2.65 (between √4 = 2 and √9 = 3 , closer to 3); ∛30 is slightly above ∛27 = 3 , so ≈ 3.1; π ≈ 3.14 . Ordering: √7 < 3 < ∛30 < π , so √7 is smallest.

steps.stem: Which of the following is closest to \(\sqrt{3}\)?
Given: \(x = \sqrt{5\,x}\). The number of solutions of the equation is —
explanation: Square both sides (valid for x ≥ 0 , which the equation requires): x² = 5x , so x² − 5x = 0 , giving x(x − 5) = 0 . Thus x = 0 or x = 5 . Both satisfy the original equation ( 0 = √0 and 5 = √25 ), so there are 2 solutions.
The principal square roots are twelve and seven, whose difference is five.
Extract the square factor thirty-six, leaving root two.
A principal square root is nonnegative. The square root of x squared is absolute x, which equals negative x when x is negative.
An odd root keeps the negative sign. Negative five cubed is negative 125.
Both sides are nonnegative, so square to get x+7=25 and x=18.
Combine the nonnegative radicands: square root 324 is eighteen.

steps.stem: Between which consecutive integers does \(\sqrt{70}\) lie?
explanation: Sixty-four is below seventy and eighty-one is above it. Their positive square roots are eight and nine.
